chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Forbearance and endurance are twins, and they are the product of high courage.

key_terms.الْحِلْمُ: Forbearance, gentleness, or patience in the face of provocation
key_terms.تَوْأَمَانِ: Twins, indicating two closely related or inseparable qualities
key_terms.عُلُوُّ الْهِمَّةِ: High aspiration, elevated courage, or lofty ambition

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between forbearance, endurance, and high aspiration in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this maxim from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies forbearance (*al-hilm*) and endurance (*al-anah*) as inseparable twins born of high aspiration (*uluw al-himmah*), a concept central to Shia ethical psychology. This teaching underscores that true patience is not passive resignation but an active, elevated state of the soul driven by lofty spiritual goals, a view emphasized by scholars like Ibn Abi al-Hadid who link it to the perfection of character (*akhlaq*).

en.sayed-ali-raza: 460. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Forbearance and endurance are twins and they are the product of high courage.
